name: BOSS
tagline: Best Order Score Search: permutation-based DAG learner using grow-shrink trees and BIC scoring on iid linear-Gaussian data.
pseudocode:
1. Initialize permutation $\pi = (1, 2, \ldots, p)$ and BIC score with grow-shrink trees per variable
2. repeat
3.   Shuffle variables $V$
4.   for each $v \in V$ do better_mutation: try inserting $v$ at every position in $\pi$, keep position with highest score
5.   end for
6. until no insertion improves the total BIC
7. Recover parents per variable from final order via $\mathrm{GST}_v.\mathrm{trace}(\pi_{<v})$
8. Convert DAG to CPDAG via $\mathrm{dag2cpdag}$
diff_from_baseline: Andrews, Ramsey, Cooper, Spirtes 2023 (NeurIPS). Permutation-based DAG search that scores each ordering via grow-shrink trees and accepts variable-position swaps as long as the BIC improves. Strong default for linear-Gaussian observational data when N >> p.

name: GRaSP
tagline: Greedy Relaxations of the Sparsest Permutation algorithm: depth-bounded DFS over orderings via covered-edge tucks.
pseudocode:
1. Initialize a random permutation $\pi$ and set parents via grow-shrink trees
2. repeat
3.   For each $(i,j)$ in $\pi$ with $j < i$ such that edge $j\to i$ is covered (or unconditionally at depth 0):
4.     Tuck: move ancestors of $\pi[i]$ up to position $j$ to form a new order
5.     Recompute local BIC on positions $j..i$; if score strictly improves, accept
6.     If score is tied, recurse depth-first up to depth $d=3$ on flipped covered edges
7.   On no improvement, revert order and continue
8. until no tuck improves the score
9. Build DAG from final $\pi$ and project to CPDAG via $\mathrm{dag2cpdag}$

key_hyperparams.name: depth
key_hyperparams.role: max DFS recursion depth over covered tucks

diff_from_baseline: Lam, Andrews, Ramsey 2022 (UAI). Permutation-search DAG learner that explores tuck-based neighborhoods by following score-equal moves under a depth bound, providing a tractable surrogate to Sparsest-Permutation search.

name: PC (constraint-based)
tagline: Classical PC algorithm: Fisher-Z conditional-independence skeleton then Meek rules to recover the CPDAG.
pseudocode:
1. Run stable skeleton discovery on $X$ using Fisher-Z $\mathrm{CIT}$ at level $\alpha=0.05$
2. Maintain separating sets for each removed edge
3. Orient unshielded colliders $a-c-b$ if $c \notin \mathrm{sepset}(a,b)$ (UC-sepset, priority 2)
4. Apply Meek rules iteratively to propagate orientations to the maximal CPDAG
5. Return the resulting GeneralGraph
diff_from_baseline: Spirtes, Glymour & Scheines, Causation, Prediction, and Search (2000). Canonical constraint-based causal discovery: skeleton via CI tests, then collider orientation and Meek propagation. Standard reference baseline for observational linear-Gaussian recovery.

name: GES
tagline: Greedy Equivalence Search: forward Insert and backward Delete operators over CPDAGs scored by BIC.
pseudocode:
1. Initialize $G$ as the empty CPDAG and compute $\mathrm{score}(G)$
2. Forward phase: while best Insert$(i,j,T)$ strictly improves BIC, apply it, project via pdag2dag and dag2cpdag
3. Each Insert respects validity tests (clique-formation $V_1$, semi-elementary chain $V_2$) and a max-parent cap $\mathrm{maxP} = N/2$
4. Backward phase: while best Delete$(i,j,H)$ strictly improves BIC, apply it and reproject to CPDAG
5. Stop when no Insert/Delete in the current equivalence class improves the score; return $G$

key_hyperparams.name: maxP
key_hyperparams.role: max parents per node in forward phase

diff_from_baseline: Chickering 2002, JMLR. Two-phase greedy CPDAG search using local BIC: forward Insert until no operator improves the score, then backward Delete. Optimal in the large-sample limit under faithfulness for linear-Gaussian models.
